product.quickSummary: This guide covers one readable legacy Sonic Braid label, SCB30040-22: 40 lb Lo-Vis Green, .25 mm and 300 yards. The label also says 10 lb test diameter, but that is a mono-equivalent comparison, not the physical diameter used here. Stren's 2014 US catalog confirms the Sonic Braid and GlideCoat family; the photographed label itself is undated.
product.suitabilityTitle: Plan a 40 lb braid working section from the actual label
product.suitabilitySummary: Use this reference when your spool matches SCB30040-22, its test rating, color and printed diameter. A 300-yard package can supply a long working section or more than one shorter fill, depending on reel capacity and reserve. Choose the amount around casting distance and the room needed to fight a fish; the package length does not mean every reel holds all 300 yards.
strengthGuide: Only the photographed 40 lb label establishes a physical diameter in this review. Other Sonic Braid strengths in historical catalogs do not inherit .25 mm.
Use .25 mm for the capacity input. The adjacent 10 lb test-diameter wording describes a monofilament comparison, not a second strength or measurement.
The supported package is 300 yards of Lo-Vis Green. Its rounded 274 m label is not converted back into a different yardage.
A later spool simply labeled Stren Braid needs its own evidence. A similar fiber or coating description does not establish formulation continuity.

spoolingGuide.title: Match the complete label
spoolingGuide.text: Look for SCB30040-22, 40 lb, .25 mm and 300 yards. The UPC on the reviewed photograph is 042083373053; a shop title or a generic Sonic product picture is not a substitute for that match.

spoolingGuide.title: Size the working section
spoolingGuide.text: Allow enough braid for the longest expected cast plus reserve for a run, trimming and retying. Use the capacity estimate to choose that section before deciding how much backing is needed.

spoolingGuide.title: Prevent spool slip
spoolingGuide.text: Follow the reel maker's braid-attachment guidance. Where required, anchor the braid over monofilament backing and keep the connection below the working section.

spoolingGuide.title: Check legacy stock before filling
spoolingGuide.text: The source does not establish manufacture date or storage condition. Inspect the line and knots, wind evenly under suitable tension, and stop at the reel's specified fill clearance.

faqs.question: Does 10 lb test diameter mean this is 10 lb braid?
faqs.answer: No. The original label identifies the braid as 40 lb. Its 10 lb test-diameter phrase is a monofilament comparison; the separate .25 mm entry is the physical diameter used for capacity.

faqs.question: Is this a 2014 diameter chart?
faqs.answer: No. The label photograph is undated. The 2014 US Stren catalog independently confirms the Sonic Braid family and construction, but its test/diameter ratios are mono-equivalent pound tests, not a physical-diameter chart.

faqs.question: Why does the linked shop title give different sizes?
faqs.answer: That listing mixes a 0.16 mm / 110 m title with images of other Sonic packages. This guide uses only the original SCB30040-22 detail label, where 40 lb, .25 mm and 300 yards are visible together.

faqs.question: Can I use this for another Sonic strength or later Stren Braid?
faqs.answer: Not without an exact label or manufacturer chart. Neither matching the brand nor a similar Dyneema description establishes the missing diameter or formulation.

faqs.question: Does a 300-yard package fit my reel?
faqs.answer: That depends on the reel's usable capacity at .25 mm and any backing. Choose a working section with enough reserve, calculate the backing, and respect the reel maker's fill clearance.
